ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in a semicircle, where $AB$ is the diameter, and the arc $DC$ is equal to the arc $CB$. If $\angle C = 110^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in a semicircle, and $\angle C=110^\circ$,
\[
\therefore \angle DAB=180^\circ-\angle C=70^\circ,
\]
since arc DC equals arc CB,
\[
\therefore CD=CB,
\]
\[
\therefore \angle CDB=\angle CBD=35^\circ,
\]
since AB is the diameter,
\[
\therefore \angle ADB=90^\circ,
\]
\[
\therefore \angle ABD=90^\circ-\angle ADB=90^\circ-70^\circ=20^\circ,
\]
\[
\therefore \angle ABC=\angle ABD+\angle CBD=20^\circ+35^\circ=\boxed{55^\circ}.
\]

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
Solution: Given that quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in a semicircle, and $\angle C=110^\circ$,
\[
\therefore \angle DAB=180^\circ-\angle C=70^\circ,
\]
since arc $DC$ equals arc $CB$,
\[
\therefore CD=CB,
\]
\[
\therefore \angle CDB=\angle CBD=35^\circ,
\]
since $AB$ is the diameter,
\[
\therefore \angle ADB=90^\circ,
\]
\[
\therefore \angle ABD=90^\circ-\angle ADB=90^\circ-70^\circ=20^\circ,
\]
\[
\therefore \angle ABC=\angle ABD+\angle CBD=20^\circ+35^\circ=\boxed{55^\circ}.
\]

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, A and B are located at the left and right endpoints of a horizontal line segment, AB is the diameter of the semicircle, and O on AB represents the center of the circle. D and C are both on the upper semicircular arc, and the order along the upper semicircle from left to right is A-D-C-B. The chords AD, DC, CB, and the diagonal DB are drawn in the figure, and C and B can be seen connected to form an angle. Reasoning: According to the radian measure method, let arc DC = arc CB = x, and let arc AD = y. Because A-D-C-B forms the upper semicircle, y + x + x = 180°. Given ∠DCB = 110°, it intercepts arc DB not containing C, and this arc is composed of arc DA plus the lower semicircular arc AB, so 110° = (y + 180°)/2, solving gives y = 40°. Thus 2x = 180° - 40° = 140°, so x = 70°. ∠ABC intercepts arc AC not containing B, namely arc AD + arc DC = 40° + 70° = 110°, therefore ∠ABC = 110°/2 = 55°.
